payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Compared with the source, does the surrounding scene read as drawn rather than retaining substantial photographic detail?
node.criteria: Pass if the surrounding scene visibly reads as drawn, with drawing-like rendering replacing substantial photographic surface detail. Fail if it retains substantial photographic representation despite added marks or stylization. Unknown only if the surrounding scene cannot be assessed.
node.source_quote: Turn the image into a drawing
node.endpoint: The surrounding scene is rendered as a drawing rather than retaining substantial photographic representation.
node.necessity: The requested transformation applies to the image as a whole; assessing the scene separately prevents a drawn-looking background from standing in for drawn main forms, or vice versa.

node_traces.evidence: Compared with the source’s detailed photographic trees, hillside, and dirt ground, the edited surrounding scene is visibly softened into broad, smudged chalk-like strokes and simplified color patches, especially across the hillside, foliage, and foreground. It no longer retains substantial photographic surface detail.

d2: The node’s criterion is broadly aligned with the requested chalk material, and the trace cites visible changes beyond generic grain. However, its pass threshold may be too permissive: the edited image retains photographic detail in the giraffes and adds strong blur/noise and smearing, which could be mistaken for chalk without establishing that the image is actually rendered as a chalk drawing. Tighten the distinction between chalk-specific surface treatment and generic filtering, and assess the image as a whole against the source. The trace’s high-confidence “pass” conflicts with the aggregate “partial” reference, but that label is not atomic ground truth: investigate whether the node is treating some chalk-like marks as complete fulfillment, and calibrate confidence to the mixed evidence rather than forcing a label. Preserve an unknown outcome for genuinely unobservable treatment; there are no transport, schema, or dependency failures indicated here.

response.content: {"text":"The node only judges the surrounding scene, so it can pass when the background looks chalk-like even though the giraffes—the dominant forms—remain substantially photographic. Keep this as a required scene-specific check, but make its criterion distinguish a coherent chalk-drawing rendering from blur, smearing, or grain alone; the trace cites softened scenery, yet does not establish that those changes amount to drawing rather than filtering. Also avoid treating this node as sufficient evidence that the whole-image request is complete: its result should be combined with a separate assessment of the main forms. The high-confidence pass versus the aggregate partial is a useful signal to inspect this threshold and confidence calibration, not proof that this node must return a particular label. Preserve unknown for genuinely unassessable scenes; the trace shows no transport, schema, or dependency failure."}
